items.title: Importing and exporting
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: Moving goods across borders adds steps and costs. Each shipment needs a customs declaration and a commodity code that classifies the goods, which decides the duty rate and any restrictions. You may owe import duty and VAT on arrival, and need a registration number to import or export (in the UK, an EORI number). Incoterms are standard shipping terms that say who pays for transport, insurance and customs at each point, and where risk passes from seller to buyer. Include duty, freight, insurance and fees in your price, or your margin disappears. A freight forwarder or customs broker can handle the paperwork.

questions.prompt: What does a commodity code do?

options.text: Classifies goods, which decides duty and any restrictions
A kind of insurance policy only
Standard shipping terms saying who pays for what and when risk passes

questions.prompt: Why include duty and freight in your selling price?

options.text: Otherwise the margin on the sale disappears
They are always paid by the customer's bank

questions.prompt: Who can help with customs paperwork?

options.text: A freight forwarder or customs broker

items.title: Fulfilling your first orders
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: Your first orders are a test of the whole process, so treat them that way. Before the first order, write down each step from enquiry to delivery and invoice: confirm the order, check stock, make or prepare, pack, send, tell the customer, invoice and collect payment. Confirm price, delivery date and what is included in writing. Keep a simple record of each order and of anything that went wrong. After delivery, ask the customer how it went and note what you would change. Fix the process before the tenth order, not after the hundredth. Heroics that work once do not scale.

questions.prompt: What should you confirm with a customer before fulfilling their first order?

options.text: Price, delivery date and what is included

questions.prompt: Why write down each step from enquiry to invoice?

options.text: So the process can be repeated and improved

questions.prompt: What should you do after the first deliveries?

options.text: Ask customers how it went and note what to change

questions.prompt: Why not rely on last-minute heroics to complete orders?

options.text: They work once and do not scale
